name: Single-leg balance
summary: Stand on one leg, hips level, and hold still.
setup: Face the phone, lift one foot a few centimetres, soft standing knee, hands free. Keep the hips level and the trunk still. Hold.
brief: Stand on one leg, the other foot a few centimetres off the floor, standing knee soft, hands free. Keep the hips level and the trunk still.
why: Facing the phone shows the trunk swaying and the pelvis dropping, so the timer runs only while you are steady. Whether the other foot is really off the floor is not checked.
progression: Eyes closed; stand on a cushion; turn the head side to side.
regression: Fingertip on a wall; shorter holds.
contraindications: Dizziness; falls risk without something to hold.

faults.label: Free-side hip dropping
faults.tip: Lift the free hip slightly; the standing hip muscles hold the pelvis level.

faults.label: Locking the standing knee
faults.tip: A slightly bent knee lets the ankle and hip do the balancing.

faults.label: Gripping with the toes
faults.tip: Clawing the toes is a sign of a wobbling ankle. Spread them and let the whole foot work.

faults.label: Eyes darting around
faults.cue: Fix your eyes on one spot
faults.tip: A steady gaze steadies the balance. Progress by closing the eyes once 30 s is easy.

guide.surface: Firm floor; a wall within reach.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the lifted foot is really off the floor.

points.t: Soft knee, foot gripping the floor.
